final_text:
## How 'Sales by month' is built (all steps backed by source files)

| # | Step | Evidence (doc_id · source_path · source_version) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The chart `SYN_CHART_ORDERED` "Sales by month" groups by `MonthStart(SalesDate)` and sums `SalesAmount`. Its label is "Sales (ordered, excluding tax)". It uses no filters and all loaded dates. | CONNECTED_c09c9d6a14cfbebb · fixtures/qlik/sales_performance.metadata.json · 8d8c9c69…55ad |
| 2 | The load script renames `ORDERDATE AS SalesDate` and `ORDERED_VALUE_EX_TAX AS SalesAmount`. It reads them from `"SYNTHETIC_SALES"."CV_ORDER_SALES"`. | CONNECTED_5a56548a8e0e4e42 · fixtures/qlik/sales_performance.qvs · 6101a40d…983e |
| 3 | In the HANA-style model CV_ORDER_SALES, there is one row per ORDERLINEID. `ORDERED_VALUE_EX_TAX = ROUND(ORDERLINES.QUANTITY * ORDERLINES.UNITPRICE, 2)` and `ORDERDATE` comes from ORDERS. It uses inner many-to-one joins: ORDERLINES→ORDERS (ORDERID), ORDERS→CUSTOMERS (CUSTOMERID) and ORDERLINES→STOCKITEMS (STOCKITEMID). | CONNECTED_c1d6c7f4b37882cd · fixtures/hana/CV_ORDER_SALES.model.xml · b2d9a0cf…684a |

**Source columns:** ORDERLINES.QUANTITY and ORDERLINES.UNITPRICE give the amount. ORDERS.ORDERDATE gives the month.

**What's missing or unconfirmed:** These are normalized synthetic fixtures. They were never run in Qlik or deployed in HANA. On the invoiced side, I took the formula from the definitions document and the reconciliation tool's description. I did not open the Spotfire source SQL (fixtures/spotfire/customer_sales.source.sql), so that path isn't traced here.

## Ordered vs. invoiced
(CONNECTED_d6d252dc2b0538ee · fixtures/business/definitions.md · 250c6d6c…da93)
- **Ordered value** is order-line quantity × unit price, dated by order date. It includes orders that have no invoice. It is a bookings measure, not revenue. This is what Qlik Sales Performance uses.
- **Invoiced sales** is invoice-line ExtendedPrice minus TaxAmount, dated by invoice date. This is what Spotfire Customer Sales uses.
- Both reports exclude tax, so tax can't explain the difference between them.

## The numbers
(ReconcileOrderedVsInvoiced, query 01c7edce-010c-6e5c-0034-28cb001b4402)

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Ordered value, all 120 orders (order dates 2026-01-03 to 2026-03-01) | 65893.02 |
| Ordered value, the 96 orders that have an invoice | 53589.47 |
| Ordered value, the 24 orders with no invoice yet | 12303.55 |
| Invoiced sales excluding tax, 96 invoices (invoice dates 2026-01-05 to 2026-03-03) | 53589.47 |

The 12303.55 difference is exactly the value of the 24 orders that have no invoice yet. For orders that do have an invoice, the ordered and invoiced amounts match exactly. Month by month, the two reports can still differ, because an order and its invoice can fall in different months. Invoice dates run about two days after order dates.

No candidate was proposed, created or released, since this request didn't involve building a product.
